input.prompt: Summarize: is Basic auth still supported on the Classic API (versions, deprecation/removal), can OAuth client credentials tokens be used on /JSSResource, Accept header for JSON.

toolu_01MqrFsNfyVAoaE3uVNgvR5B.prompt: Summarize: is Basic auth still supported on the Classic API (versions, deprecation/removal), can OAuth client credentials tokens be used on /JSSResource, Accept header for JSON.

content.content:
**Token URL:** Clients obtain an access token from `/api/oauth/token`, using the Client ID and Client Secret.

**Token lifetime default:** The article doesn't state a default. It says the response's `expires_in` value gives the number of seconds until the token expires. When creating an API Client, you can set the access token lifetime in seconds, but no default value is given.

**Client secret:**
- The secret is shown only when it's generated, so store it in a password manager. The article says there is "no way to retrieve an existing Client Secret, neither via the GUI nor the API."
- Expired tokens can't be extended. You must use the Client ID and Secret to request a new token.
- Once you've used a token, the article recommends invalidating it using the token itself.

**Role changes:**
- Adding or removing an API Role from a client is a "scope change" and requires a new Client Secret.
- Changing the privileges within an existing API Role takes effect immediately, without a new secret.
- The article recommends creating a dedicated API Role for each API Client instead of sharing roles across clients.

**Disabling clients:**
- API Clients can be set to enabled or disabled through the API, but the article doesn't describe a procedure for disabling one.
- The article says it's not currently possible to disable API access for user accounts using Bearer Token Authentication.

**Basic auth:** Still supported, but only to obtain a Bearer Token from `/v1/auth/token`, which was added in 10.42.0.
- Before 11.5.0, Basic auth could call any Classic API endpoint.
- From 11.5.0, username and password can only obtain a token.
- Starting with Jamf Pro "11.17.0," Basic auth can't be used for anything except getting an access token. Before 11.17.0, admins could enable or disable this in the UI.
- On servers that have disabled it, using Basic auth on other endpoints returns a 401 Unauthorized response.
- The article doesn't say Basic auth is being removed entirely.

**Client credentials on /JSSResource:** Client credentials support was added to the Classic API in 10.49.0. The article doesn't mention `/JSSResource` specifically, so it doesn't confirm whether these tokens work on that path.

**Accept header for JSON:** The article doesn't cover this.

The search turned up official Jamf documentation plus community and vendor posts about the bypass option and the failover URL.

- **Official docs:** Jamf's SSO setup guide describes a Failover Login URL that you copy from the SSO settings and save somewhere secure. It lets you sign in with your Jamf Pro credentials after SSO is enabled. The bypass option itself allows users to sign in to Jamf Pro without SSO, if they directly navigate to the Jamf Pro URL.
- **Current label:** Jamf's SAML guide refers to the checkbox as "Allow users to bypass the Single Sign-On authentication," not "Allow bypass for all users." That older wording appears in a Duo integration guide, which also notes that if you enable the "Allow bypass for all users" option then your JSS users may continue to login without Duo authentication.
- **Regenerating the URL:** A Jamf community post says the failover URL can be unique to your instance, and that you can regenerate it from the Single Sign-On settings using the edit and regenerate controls.
- **Security concern:** Community users have raised concerns that the failover login path lets someone sign in with only a username and password, bypassing SSO and MFA. One thread asks how to block it. A third-party vendor's doc calls the `?failover` approach undocumented and warns that Jamf may discontinue the '?failover' parameter without notice.

Caveat: these results are mostly community forum posts and third-party docs. I didn't verify the current Jamf Pro UI wording or whether the `?failover` behavior has changed in recent versions, so check the official Jamf Pro documentation for your version before relying on it.

content.text:
# Jamf Pro read-only API research for the Maester Pack connector (checks 1–13)

Researched 2026-11-09. The published Jamf Pro API spec is version **11.33.0**, for example `"version": "11.33.0"` in https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v4-computers-inventory.md.

## Conventions

- **JPAPI** means the Jamf Pro API, at `{server}/api/...`. **Classic** means `{server}/JSSResource/...`.
- **Privilege table.** The JPAPI privilege names and deprecation dates come from https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/privileges-and-deprecations (cited below as **[PD]**).
- **Classic privileges.** The Classic API privilege names come from https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-minimum-required-privileges-and-endpoint-mapping (cited as **[CP]**). That page writes them in the user-account style, for example "Read - Webhooks".
- **Exact API role strings.** The privilege string an API role uses for a Classic endpoint (for example "Read Webhooks" or "Read macOS Configuration Profiles") is UNVERIFIED. Check it against `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges`.
- **Paging, sort and filter.** Paged JPAPI endpoints share the same parameters: `page` (default 0), `page-size` (default 100), `sort=prop:asc|desc` (comma-separated), and `filter=<RSQL>`.
- **RSQL syntax.** The operators are `==` `!=` `=lt=` `=le=` `=gt=` `=ge=` `=in=` `=out=`. `;` means AND and `,` means OR. `*` is a wildcard with `==` and `!=`. String comparisons ignore case. Null values never match a comparison. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/filtering-with-rsql.md

---

## 0. Authentication, token lifetime, invalidation, rate limits, and cloud versus on-prem

### Token request

- **Endpoint.** The current spec documents `POST {server}/api/v1/oauth/token` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
  - Form fields: `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and an optional `scope` such as `api-role:1 api-role:2`.
  - Response: `access_token` (string, JWT), `token_type` ("Bearer"), `scope` (string), `expires_in` (integer seconds, taken from the client's `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds`).
  - A 400 uses the OAuth2 error format (`error`, `error_description`, `error_uri`).
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md
  - The spec's securityScheme `tokenUrl` is `/api/v1/oauth/token` (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-notifications.md). Jamf's recipe also uses `${url}/api/v1/oauth/token` (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/recipes/client-credentials-authorization.md).
- **Legacy path.** Jamf's blog documents `/api/oauth/token` (https://www.jamf.com/blog/understanding-jamf-pro-api-roles-and-clients/). Recommendation: use `/api/v1/oauth/token`. Whether `/api/oauth/token` still works on 11.33 is UNVERIFIED.
- **Version support.** Client credentials work on both the Classic API and the JPAPI from 10.49.0. "Access tokens can be used to interact with API endpoints in both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs." Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/client-credentials.md

### Roles, secrets and lifetime

- **Role and secret changes.** Adding or removing an API role on a client requires rotating the client secret. Changing the privileges inside a role takes effect for new tokens straight away. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/client-credentials.md
- **Secret retrieval.** A secret cannot be read back through the UI or the API. Source: the Jamf blog above.
- **Default lifetime.** The default `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds` is UNVERIFIED. Third parties cite 1800 seconds, but no primary source confirms it.

### Invalidation

- **Endpoint.** `POST /api/v1/auth/invalidate-token` with a Bearer token returns 204 "token invalidated". No privilege is needed.
  - Sources: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/post_v1-auth-invalidate-token.md and [PD].
  - Jamf's client-credentials recipe calls this endpoint with a client-credentials token, so it works for OAuth tokens. Source: the recipe URL above.
  - The legacy `POST /auth/invalidateToken` was deprecated on 2020-06-01 [PD].
- **Basic auth.** From 11.5.0, a username and password can only obtain a token. From 11.17.0 that restriction is mandatory. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-authentication-changes.md
- **SSO.** API authentication does not support SSO. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-pro-api-overview.md

### Rate limits

- **No built-in limit.** "Jamf Pro does not have a built-in solution to restrict or limit the number of API requests."
- **Guidance.** Use no more than **5 concurrent connections**, measure response times, and use exponential backoff. Run a full inventory sync no more than once every 24 hours, and filter on `general.reportDate`.
- Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-pro-api-scalability-best-practices.md
- **Load signal on Jamf Cloud.** `GET /api/v1/health-status` returns acceptance ratios from 0 to 1 per concurrency group (`api`, `ui`, `enrollment`, `device`, `default`). Each group has the fields `thirtySeconds`, `oneMinute`, `fiveMinutes`, `fifteenMinutes`, `thirtyMinutes`.
  - "Health status metrics are only available in Jamf Cloud." On-prem returns 404. The page lists no 429 response.
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-health-status.md

### Cloud versus on-prem

- **Detection.** `GET /api/v1/cloud-information` needs no authentication (`x-authentication-required: false`). It returns `{cloudInstance, rampInstance, fedRampInstance, govCloudInstance, managedServiceProviderInstance, highComplianceInstance, fipsEnabled}`, all booleans. Use it to tell Jamf Cloud from on-prem. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-cloud-information.md
- **Clustering.** Jamf Cloud is clustered and the cluster refreshes every minute. A newly created object can take up to 60 seconds to reach the other nodes. Sticky sessions use the `APBALANCEID` or `jpro-ingress` cookie, but are only needed for create-then-use workflows, so a read-only pack does not need them. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/sticky-sessions-for-jamf-cloud.md
- **Change Management export.** Only on-prem can write logs to a file or syslog. See section 12.

---

## 1. SSO settings

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v3/sso`
- **Privilege:** **Read SSO Settings** ([PD]; https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-sso.md)
- **Top-level fields (`SsoSettingsV3`):**
  - `configurationType`: enum `SAML`, `OIDC`, `OIDC_WITH_SAML`
  - `ssoEnabled`: boolean
  - `ssoBypassAllowed`: boolean
  - `ssoForEnrollmentEnabled`: boolean
  - `ssoForMacOsSelfServiceEnabled`: boolean
  - `enrollmentSsoForAccountDrivenEnrollmentEnabled`: boolean
  - `groupEnrollmentAccessEnabled`: boolean
  - `groupEnrollmentAccessName`: string
  - `enrollmentSsoConfig`: `{hosts: [string], managementHint}`
- **`oidcSettings`:** `userMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`), `jamfIdAuthenticationEnabled` (boolean, default true), `usernameAttributeClaimMapping`
- **`samlSettings`:**
  - `idpProviderType`: enum `ADFS`, `OKTA`, `GOOGLE`, `SHIBBOLETH`, `ONELOGIN`, `PING`, `CENTRIFY`, `AZURE`, `OTHER`
  - `metadataSource`: enum `URL`, `FILE`, `UNKNOWN`
  - `sessionTimeout`: int, default 480
  - `tokenExpirationDisabled`: boolean
  - also `idpUrl`, `entityId`, `userMapping`, `groupAttributeName`, `userAttributeEnabled`
- **What `ssoBypassAllowed` means:** the spec does not define the field. Jamf's documentation describes the checkbox as "Allow users to bypass the Single Sign-On authentication", which lets users sign in without SSO when they go straight to the Jamf Pro URL. Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Enabling_Single_Sign-On_in_Jamf_Pro (from search results). The link between the field and the checkbox is an inference; treat it as UNVERIFIED-strong.
- **Failover login:** `GET /api/v1/sso/failover` returns `{failoverUrl: string, generationTime: int64}`, or a 400 "Failover url not generated". Privilege: **Read SSO Settings**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-sso-failover.md
  - Failover always lets a local account sign in with a password. A check can report that this exists, but cannot turn it off.
- **Related:** `GET /api/v2/jamf-pro-information` returns `ssoSamlEnabled` and needs no named privilege. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v2-jamf-pro-information.md
- **Sample:**
  `{"configurationType":"SAML","ssoEnabled":true,"ssoBypassAllowed":false,"ssoForEnrollmentEnabled":true,"samlSettings":{"idpProviderType":"AZURE","sessionTimeout":480,"tokenExpirationDisabled":false},"oidcSettings":{"userMapping":"USERNAME"}}`

## 2. API roles

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/api-roles`, and `/{id}` for one role
- **Privilege:** **Read API Roles** ([PD]; https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/getallapiroles.md)
- **Paging, sort and filter:** page, page-size=100, `sort` default `id:asc` (fields `id`, `displayName`), `filter` on `id` and `displayName`, for example `displayName=="*myRole*"`
- **Response:** `{totalCount: int, results: [{id: string, displayName: string, privileges: [string]}]}`
- **Catalogue of all privileges:** `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges` returns `{privileges: [string]}` (sorted). Privilege: **Read API Roles**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-api-role-privileges.md
- **Sample:** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":"1","displayName":"Maester RO","privileges":["Read Computers","Read SSO Settings"]}]}`

## 3. API integrations (API clients)

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/api-integrations`, and `/{id}` for one client
- **Privilege:** **Read API Integrations** ([PD]; https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-api-integrations.md)
- **Paging, sort and filter:** `sort` default `id:asc`; sort and filter fields are `id` and `displayName`
- **Fields:**
  - `id`: integer
  - `displayName`: string
  - `enabled`: boolean
  - `authorizationScopes`: [string], the names of the assigned API roles
  - `appType`: enum `CLIENT_CREDENTIALS`, `NATIVE_APP_OAUTH`, `NONE`
  - `clientId`: string
  - `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds`: integer, optional
- **Created and last-used dates:** neither exists in the schema (same source). There is also no secret-age field.
- **Sample:** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":1,"displayName":"My API Integration","enabled":true,"authorizationScopes":["Maester RO"],"accessTokenLifetimeSeconds":300,"appType":"CLIENT_CREDENTIALS","clientId":"538878d4-..."}]}`

## 4. Jamf Pro user accounts and groups

### Accounts

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/accounts`
- **Privilege:** **Read Accounts** ([PD]; https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-accounts.md)
- **Sort and filter fields:** `id`, `lastPasswordChange`, `failedLoginAttempts`, `username`, `realname`, `email`, `phone`, `ldapServerId`, `distinguishedName`, `siteId`, `privilegeLevel`, `changePasswordOnNextLogin`, `accountStatus`. The default sort is `username:asc`; the description says `:desc`, so the spec is inconsistent.
- **Fields:**
  - `id`: string
  - `username`, `realname`, `email`, `phone`: string
  - `ldapServerId`: int, default -1. A value of -1 means a local account; this is inferred from the default.
  - `distinguishedName`: string
  - `siteId`: int
  - `accessLevel`: enum `FullAccess`, `SiteAccess`, `GroupBasedAccess`
  - `privilegeLevel`: enum `ADMINISTRATOR`, `AUDITOR`, `ENROLLMENT`, `CUSTOM`
  - `lastPasswordChange`: date-time
  - `changePasswordOnNextLogin`: boolean
  - `failedLoginAttempts`: int
  - `accountStatus`: enum `Enabled`, `Disabled`
  - `accountType`: enum `DEFAULT`, `FEDERATED`, `MIGRATED`
- **Example filters:** `privilegeLevel==ADMINISTRATOR;accountStatus==Enabled`, or `ldapServerId==-1` for local accounts
- **Sample:** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":"1","username":"admin","ldapServerId":-1,"siteId":-1,"accessLevel":"FullAccess","privilegeLevel":"ADMINISTRATOR","lastPasswordChange":"2017-07-21T17:32:28Z","changePasswordOnNextLogin":false,"failedLoginAttempts":0,"accountStatus":"Enabled","accountType":"DEFAULT"}]}`

### Groups

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/account-groups`
- **Privilege:** **Read Account Groups** ([PD]; https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-account-groups.md)
- **Sort and filter fields:** `id`, `name`, `siteId`, `ldapServerId`
- **Fields:** `id`, `name`, `accessLevel`, `privilegeLevel` (same enums as accounts), `siteId` (string), `ldapServerId` (string), `directoryGroupId`, `members: [{id, username, realname, email}]`, `privileges: [string]`

### Last login

- **Per-account:** no last-login field exists on `UserAccount`.
- **`GET /api/v1/last-login`:** privilege **Read Last Login**. Returns `{lastLogin: date-time}`, or 204 when no data exists. It takes no parameters, and the docs do not say whose login it reports (UNVERIFIED). Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-last-login.md
- **`GET /api/v1/user-sessions/active`:** privilege **Read User**. Returns `[{username, sessionId, lastAccessedTime, creationTime, userAgent, ipAddress}]`. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-user-sessions-active.md

### Classic alternative (not needed)

## 5. Console password policy and lockout

- **No API endpoint was found.** Neither the JPAPI index (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/jamf-pro-api/llms.txt) nor the Classic index (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/classic-api/llms.txt) has a password-policy or lockout resource. Any such endpoint is UNVERIFIED and probably does not exist.
- **Account preferences are not the policy.** `/api/v2/account-preferences` and `/api/v3/account-preferences` (no privilege; v2 deprecated 2025-06-30 [PD]) hold the caller's own UI preferences: language, timezone, theme, search methods. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-account-preferences.md
- **What the policy covers in the UI.** It sets lockout attempts, self-unlock, password length, age, reuse and complexity. It applies only to local accounts, not to SSO, directory or cloud IdP accounts. Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-11.16.0/Configuring_the_Password_Policy
- **Possible proxy signals:** `failedLoginAttempts`, `lastPasswordChange` and `changePasswordOnNextLogin` on `/api/v1/accounts`.
- **STIG values** (Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG V3R2, published 2026-09-02):
  - V-241804: password length of 15
  - V-241805 to V-241808: lowercase, uppercase, number and special character
  - V-241809 and V-241810: minimum lifetime 24 hours, maximum lifetime 6 months
  - V-241811: no reuse for 5 generations
  - V-241812: disable after 35 days inactive
  - V-241813: lock after 3 invalid attempts
  - Source: https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2

## 9. Computer configuration profiles

- **Classic only.** No JPAPI endpoint lists or reads macOS configuration profiles; the JPAPI index has no such section (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/jamf-pro-api/llms.txt).
- **List:** `GET /JSSResource/osxconfigurationprofiles` returns `os_x_configuration_profiles: [{id, name}]`. Send `Accept: application/json` to get JSON instead of XML. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findosxconfigurationprofiles.md
- **Detail:** `GET /JSSResource/osxconfigurationprofiles/id/{id}` returns:
  - `general{id, name, uuid, distribution_method ("Install Automatically"|"Make Available in Self Service"), user_removable, level ("computer"|"user"), redeploy_on_update, payloads (string)}`
  - `scope{all_computers (bool), all_jss_users, computers, computer_groups, buildings, departments, jss_users, jss_user_groups, limitations{...}, exclusions{computers, computer_groups, ...}}`
  - `self_service{...}`
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findosxconfigurationprofilesbyid.md
- **Privilege:** "Read - macOS Configuration Profiles" [CP]. The API role string is presumably "Read macOS Configuration Profiles" (UNVERIFIED).
- **Paging:** none, so the pack needs one call per profile (N+1 calls).
- **Payloads:** `payloads` is a string. That it holds an XML plist is UNVERIFIED in the spec but standard. Parse it and match `PayloadType`:
  - FileVault: `com.apple.MCX.FileVault2` (keys `Enable`, `Defer`, `ShowRecoveryKey`, `UseRecoveryKey`, ...); escrow: `com.apple.security.FDERecoveryKeyEscrow`. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicemanagement/fdefilevault and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicemanagement/fderecoverykeyescrow
  - Firewall: `com.apple.security.firewall` (keys `EnableFirewall`, `BlockAllIncoming`, `EnableStealthMode`). Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicemanagement/firewall
  - Gatekeeper: `com.apple.systempolicy.control` (keys `EnableAssessment`, `AllowIdentifiedDevelopers`, `EnableXProtectMalwareUpload`). Source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicemanagement/systempolicycontrol
- **"Scoped to all computers"** means `scope.all_computers == true`, or a scoped group that covers every computer, which needs judgement. Also check that `scope.exclusions` is empty.
- **FileVault settings objects:** Classic `/JSSResource/diskencryptionconfigurations` ("Read - Disk Encryption Configurations" [CP]) holds the FileVault configurations used by policies.
- **Mobile profiles:** `/JSSResource/mobiledeviceconfigurationprofiles`, "Read - Mobile Device Configuration Profiles" [CP].

## 10. Computer inventory

- **Current endpoint:** `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory`
  - **Privilege:** **Read Computers**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v4-computers-inventory.md
  - `/api/v3/computers-inventory` is marked `deprecated: true` with `x-deprecation-date: 2026-07-14` in https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-computers-inventory.md
  - Earlier versions: v1 deprecated 2025-06-30, v2 deprecated 2025-11-06 [PD]. Classic `/JSSResource/computers` deprecated 2025-02-11 [CP].
- **Parameters:**
  - `section` (repeatable): `GENERAL`, `DISK_ENCRYPTION`, `SECURITY`, `OPERATING_SYSTEM`, `HARDWARE`, `CONFIGURATION_PROFILES`, `SOFTWARE_UPDATES`, `LOCAL_USER_ACCOUNTS`, `GROUP_MEMBERSHIPS`, ...
  - `page`, `page-size` (default 100). The spec states no maximum, so the maximum page size is UNVERIFIED.
  - `sort` (default `general.name:asc`)
  - `filter` (RSQL)
- **Filterable fields of interest:**
  - `general.lastContact`, `general.reportDate`, `general.remoteManagement.managed`, `general.supervised`, `general.userApprovedMdm`, `general.enrolledViaAutomatedDeviceEnrollment`
  - `operatingSystem.version`, `operatingSystem.fileVault2Status`
  - `diskEncryption.fileVault2Enabled`
  - `security.firewallEnabled`, `security.activationLockEnabled`, `security.recoveryLockEnabled`, `security.lockdownModeEnabled`
  - Note: there is no `lastContactTime`; the field is **`general.lastContact`**. The sort list names `general.mdmCertificateExpiration`, but the schema has `mdmProfileExpiration`.
- **GENERAL fields:** `lastContact` (date-time), `lastEnrolledDate`, `reportDate`, `remoteManagement.managed` (boolean), `mdmCapable.capable`, `supervised`, `userApprovedMdm`, `enrolledViaAutomatedDeviceEnrollment`
- **OPERATING_SYSTEM fields:** `version`, `build`, `fileVault2Status` (enum `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `NOT_ENCRYPTED`, `BOOT_ENCRYPTED`, `SOME_ENCRYPTED`, `ALL_ENCRYPTED`)
- **DISK_ENCRYPTION fields:**
  - `individualRecoveryKeyValidityStatus`: enum `VALID`, `INVALID`, `UNKNOWN`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`. This shows whether the personal recovery key is escrowed and valid.
  - `institutionalRecoveryKeyPresent`: boolean
  - `diskEncryptionConfigurationName`
  - `fileVault2EnabledUserNames`: [string]
  - `bootPartitionEncryptionDetails.partitionFileVault2State`: enum `ENCRYPTED`, `ENCRYPTING`, `UNENCRYPTED`, `DECRYPTED`, ...
- **SECURITY fields:**
  - `sipStatus`: enum `NOT_COLLECTED`, `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `DISABLED`, `ENABLED`
  - `gatekeeperStatus`: enum `NOT_COLLECTED`, `DISABLED`, `APP_STORE_AND_IDENTIFIED_DEVELOPERS`, `APP_STORE`
  - `firewallEnabled`, `autoLoginDisabled`, `remoteDesktopEnabled`, `activationLockEnabled`, `recoveryLockEnabled`, `bootstrapTokenAllowed`: boolean
  - `secureBootLevel`: enum `FULL_SECURITY`, `MEDIUM_SECURITY`, `NO_SECURITY`, ...
  - `externalBootLevel`: enum
  - `bootstrapTokenEscrowedStatus`: enum `ESCROWED`, `NOT_ESCROWED`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`
  - `xprotectVersion`: string
- **Do not use:** `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/filevault` returns the recovery key itself and needs **View Disk Encryption Recovery Key** [PD]. A read-only role should not include that privilege.
- **Example request:**
  `GET /api/v4/computers-inventory?section=GENERAL&section=OPERATING_SYSTEM&section=DISK_ENCRYPTION&section=SECURITY&page=0&page-size=100&filter=general.remoteManagement.managed==true`
- **Sample response:**
  `{"totalCount":2,"results":[{"id":"1","general":{"name":"Mac-01","lastContact":"2026-11-08T10:00:00Z","remoteManagement":{"managed":true}},"operatingSystem":{"version":"26.1","fileVault2Status":"ALL_ENCRYPTED"},"diskEncryption":{"individualRecoveryKeyValidityStatus":"VALID"},"security":{"sipStatus":"ENABLED","gatekeeperStatus":"APP_STORE_AND_IDENTIFIED_DEVELOPERS","firewallEnabled":true}}]}`

## 12. Audit and change management

- **Change Management:** no API was found for its settings or logs in either index. Source: the llms.txt indexes above.
  - On-prem can write `JAMFChangeManagement.log` and send to syslog. On Jamf Cloud, changes "cannot be exported", meaning they appear only in the UI. Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Change_Management
  - Jamf Log Stream for Cloud Premium sends logs to Splunk, S3, Datadog or HTTPS (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-log-stream). An API to check whether it is configured is UNVERIFIED.
  - STIG V-241793 requires that logs be transferred to another server.
- **Log flushing (retention):** `GET /api/v1/log-flushing` returns `{retentionPolicies: [{displayName, qualifier, retentionPeriod: int, retentionPeriodUnit: "DAY|WEEK|MONTH|YEAR"}], hourOfDay: int}`. Privilege: **Read Retention Policy**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-log-flushing.md
- **Webhooks (Classic only):**
  - `GET /JSSResource/webhooks` returns `[{id, name}]`
  - `/webhooks/id/{id}` returns `{id, name, enabled, url, content_type, event (enum, for example ComputerAdded or RestAPIOperation), connection_timeout, read_timeout, authentication_type (NONE|BASIC), username, ...}`
  - Privilege: "Read - Webhooks" [CP]
  - Sources: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findwebhooks.md and https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findwebhooksbyid.md
  - Checks this enables: webhook URLs that are not HTTPS, and `authentication_type == NONE`.
- **Object history:** `/v1/device-enrollments/{id}/history`, `/v1/jamf-pro-server-url/history` and others exist per object [PD].
- **Health notifications:** `GET /api/v1/notifications` (no named privilege) returns `[{type, id, params}]`. The `type` enum includes `INSECURE_LDAP`, `PUSH_CERT_WILL_EXPIRE`, `PUSH_CERT_EXPIRED`, `DEP_INSTANCE_WILL_EXPIRE`, `SSO_CERT_WILL_EXPIRE`, `SSO_IDP_CERT_WILL_EXPIRE`, `TOMCAT_SSL_CERT_WILL_EXPIRE`, `VPP_TOKEN_REVOKED`, `USER_INITIATED_ENROLLMENT_MANAGEMENT_ACCOUNT_SECURITY_ISSUE`, `POLICY_MANAGEMENT_ACCOUNT_PAYLOAD_SECURITY_*`, `SAML_RESPONSE_ASSERTION_SIGNING_REQUIRED`.
  - The notifications are scoped "for user and site". Whether an API client sees them is UNVERIFIED.
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-notifications.md

## 13. Server URL and token invalidation

- **Server URL:** `GET /api/v1/jamf-pro-server-url` returns `{url: string}`. Privilege: **Read JSS URL**. The index lists it under the section name "jamf-pro-server-url-preview". Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-jamf-pro-server-url.md
- **Token invalidation:** see section 0. Call `POST /api/v1/auth/invalidate-token` at the end of a run; it returns 204. `POST /api/v1/auth/keep-alive` exists but is not needed for client credentials; request a new token instead.
